This form documents the data and code supporting the computational findings in
the article and describes how to reproduce those findings.

# Part 1: Data

- [ ] This paper does not involve analysis of external data.

- [x] I certify that the authors have legitimate access to and permission to
  use the data analyzed in this manuscript.

## Abstract

The empirical analyses use two public data sources and one author-generated
synthetic benchmark. The EPA study analyzes 2,814 collocated air-sensor
site-days. The VitalDB study analyzes one matched pulse-oximetry and
arterial-blood-gas pair for each of 3,178 subjects. The synthetic study contains
6,000 evaluation dossiers, of which 5,997 have valid automated scores; the
primary analysis uses 2,998 cases from Corpus A. Simulation outputs and derived
data supporting all reported figures and tables accompany the submission.

# Part 2: Code

## Abstract

The supplied R package and analysis scripts implement the proposed local-CDF
estimators, adaptive borrowing criterion, simulation designs, multiplier
procedures, empirical analyses, and generation of manuscript tables and
figures. Python code retrieves and matches the public VitalDB measurements.
Shell and R entry points validate the numerical evidence and rebuild all
manuscript displays. Unit tests cover the estimator, sample splitting,
simulation design, application helpers, and claim-to-result correspondence.

#### Libraries and dependencies used by the code

### Supporting system/hardware requirements

The release was validated on Apple Silicon running macOS 15.4.1. No GPU is
required. The presentation-only rebuild runs on a standard desktop. Full Monte
Carlo recomputation benefits from multiple CPU cores and substantial elapsed
time but does not require a computing cluster.

# Part 3: Reproducibility workflow

## Scope

The provided workflow reproduces:

- [x] Any numbers provided in text in the paper.
- [x] The computational methods presented in the paper.
- [x] All tables and figures in the paper.
- [ ] Selected tables and figures only.

## Workflow

### Location

- [x] As part of the paper's supplementary material.
- [ ] In a Git repository disclosed during anonymous review.
- [ ] Other.

The anonymous supplementary archive is self-contained for source inspection,
tests, reconstruction of manuscript-facing tables and figures, and staged
recomputation. A public repository location can be added to the accepted
version of this form after peer review without changing the workflow.

### Format(s)

- [x] Single master code file.
- [x] Wrapper shell script(s).
- [ ] Self-contained Quarto, R Markdown, or Jupyter notebook.
- [x] Text file that documents the workflow.
- [x] Makefile.
- [x] Other: an R package with unit tests and staged analysis scripts.

### Instructions

From the root of the uncompressed anonymous supplementary archive:

1. Review `reproducibility/ANONYMOUS_REVIEW_README.md` and `renv.lock`.
2. Restore the R environment if desired with `renv::restore()` and install the
   Python figure dependencies from
   `reproducibility/requirements-figures.txt`.
3. Rebuild every main figure, the fixed-sample Supplement figure, the three
   main tables, and Supplement Tables S5--S6 with:

   ```sh
   bash reproducibility/rebuild_submission_artifacts.sh
   ```

4. Run the implementation, design-correspondence, and claim-to-evidence checks
   with:

   ```sh
   Rscript reproducibility/run_correspondence_gate.R
   ```

5. Inspect the complete ordered recomputation plan without changing any result
   file with:

   ```sh
   Rscript reproduce.R 4 all
   ```

6. Full recomputation is staged by simulation, application, and AI components.
   The exact execution and finalization commands are documented in
   `docs/CANONICAL_RECOMPUTATION_PLAN.md`. The AI stage uses the supplied
   automated scores and does not call the external scoring service. After a
   full recomputation, `reproducibility/validate_frozen_results.R` checks the
   complete result store.

### Expected run-time

Approximate time needed to reproduce the analyses on a standard desktop
machine:

- [ ] < 1 minute.
- [ ] 1-10 minutes.
- [ ] 10-60 minutes.
- [ ] 1-8 hours.
- [x] > 8 hours.
- [ ] Not feasible to run on a desktop machine.

The display rebuild in Step 3 completes in less than one minute in the
validated environment. Full Monte Carlo recomputation takes more than eight
hours and is organized into independent stages. The supplied numerical
results allow every reported table and figure to be rebuilt without rerunning
the full Monte Carlo program.

### Additional information

`README.md`, `reproducibility/README.md`,
`docs/CANONICAL_RECOMPUTATION_PLAN.md`, and the package tests document the
workflow and provide smaller checks of the proposed methods. The anonymous
archive omits author identities, affiliations, private local paths, and API
credentials; the complete unblinded archive is retained separately for the
editors.
